items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1957-08-04
items.q: then he went and played with Joe Petit. That's his first job with cornet out there.

ctx.x: Yes, I knew him. He was a travel player.

He was a travel player. Yes. And, but nevertheless, he used to, after he quit the job, well, I'd taken his job on Rylan and Beaville at Mr. Michel. It's a juror store. And when he left from there, he started playing. My daddy bought him a little brass cornet. Then he started learning that and then he went and played with Joe Petit. That's his first job with cornet out there. After he left Bally, he said that he told my mother and father that he could not be heard and he wanted to get a cornet. So he takes my dad…
He gave up the violin. He gave up the violin. When did he play on the mandolin? He said he was the first.
